items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I went back to the hotel and told John L. what had happened... John L. told me that I could sleep in his room with him until the money came.

ctx.x: Would Charlie wait for me was the question I kept asking myself as I put on my clothes as fast as I could. The bus was leaving from 'Ann Montgomery's' place as we had rooms upstairs over the club. The hotel where John L. lived was two blocks from 'Ann's' place and when I came out of the hotel and looked up the street, I got the answer; the bus was not there. Had the bus driver gone to gas up and come back to the hotel?

That question was answered when I arrived at 'Ann's' place and was told that Charlie had waited for me until 15 minuted before I arrived. I had spent most of the money I had the night before, so I went back to the hotel and told John L. what had happened. I had left New York being owed a week's salary by Bobby Neal which he had not paid me when I left his orchestra and I had not bothered to collect it because I could trust Bobby and knew that I would get the loot whenever I asked him for it.
